TMax-15K.reason: Unify CSV, JSON and Parquet telemetry with varying column names into one pipeline: the same three formats and the same field-mapping problem.
Consolidate CSV and JSONL user data into one Parquet file without duplicate or stale records; same output format and dedupe-on-key discipline.
Merge a Parquet user table with regional CSVs in different encodings on user_id; multi-format join with encoding and type pitfalls.
Three upstream feeds in three formats with slightly different schemas, orchestrated into one clean dataset; same schema-reconciliation core.
Legacy systems dump configs in different formats and schemas; normalise, deduplicate and write a canonical record set. Same shape, config domain.
Three raw files in different formats with duplicate records from retried ETL; identify and collapse duplicates across sources.
Explicit multi-format read plus schema unification of two channel datasets before aggregation; the field-mapping half of the TB2.1 task.
Clean, deduplicate and merge daily user dumps and activity logs through a scripted pipeline; merge-on-key with duplicate handling.
Unify a SQLite database with a JSON document store to find violations; joining records across storage formats with different schemas.
Debug an ETL script that merges two CSVs and saves to Parquet; touches the same merge-then-write-Parquet path but the bug is elsewhere.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Merge a base spec with host-specific overrides, deduplicate per explicit rules and emit a canonical document: priority-based conflict resolution, JSON instead of Parquet.
Same base-plus-overrides merge with uniqueness rules and a canonical deduplicated output plus checksum; overrides beat base exactly like source_a beats source_b.
Produce dedup_audit.json listing duplicated entries with occurrence counts alongside a normalised canonical file; the conflict-report-plus-merged-output pair.
Merge alias definitions from JSON into an existing config while preserving existing entries; merge with a precedence rule and a report.
Dedup audit that isolates exactly the duplicate entries removed with counts, plus a normalised canonical file; conflict accounting must be internally consistent.
Schema-validate two CSVs, join them and emit inspection plus aggregation reports; validate-map-join-report is the same pipeline skeleton.
Detect and correct schema-violating rows before joining two CSVs; the data-quality gate that precedes any honest merge.
Join two files into one output after applying documented data-quality guidelines, with the originals archived first; join under stated rules.
Clean an expected-file manifest then reconcile actual files against it and report the differences; reconciliation reporting, no schema mapping.
Read a gzipped VCF and a Parquet file and count records from each; only the read-two-different-formats step transfers.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Combine two CSVs with different column names into one per-area statistics table; field mapping plus join into a single output file.
Read a gzipped VCF and a Parquet file and emit a typed JSON result; multi-format ingestion with an exactly-typed report, strongly verified.
Convert newline-delimited JSON to CSV and then to a typed SQLite table; format conversion chain with schema declared along the way.
Produce a structured difference report between two JSON documents in several formats; per-key conflict enumeration, like conflicts.json.
Dump every table of a SQLite database into one nested JSON object keyed by table; schema-driven serialisation to an exact structure.
Reshape a CSV into a different row/column layout with exact formatting; pure format transformation, single source.
Parse a CSV into a nested dictionary keyed in a specified order; record restructuring without merging or conflicts.
Extract API data into two JSON files with exactly specified object shapes; producing several pinned structured artifacts.
Build a typed record with declared field types and serialise to JSON; only the schema-declaration-then-emit step transfers.
Store JSON records in a database with a generated column derived from a JSON field; mapping semi-structured data onto typed columns.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: Parquet round-trip loses timezone/timestamp resolution: exactly the type-and-date fidelity that the merged Parquet output must preserve.
Parquet column filtering breaks on NoneType with the pandas backend; nulls in Parquet columns are the merger's main dtype hazard.
Parser silently returns None when given multiple candidate formats; parsing dates that arrive in several formats is the TB2.1 normalisation step.
parse_date raises KeyError on unsigned dates; ISO-8601 date parsing correctness, which the YYYY-MM-DD requirement depends on.
Broken equality and length semantics in deepdiff's set type; the library whose job is enumerating differences between two records.
pd.concat is broken by removed assignments; concatenating frames from several sources is step one of the merge.
DateTime field mishandles oversized timestamps; coercing incoming date values into a declared schema type.
json_schema() emits invalid output for None values; declaring and validating a target schema, including how null is represented.
Missing DateTimeFormatter.format method; the output-side of date normalisation in the same date library.
get_engine in the parquet module raises NameError for some engines; Parquet engine plumbing, shallower than the fidelity bugs above.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Allow importing ragged CSV whose rows have unequal width; handling sources whose shape does not match the declared schema, in a multi-format tabular library.
xlsx exports with unpopulated columns now fail with InvalidDimensions; the same ingest-a-source-with-missing-fields problem.
read_json turns large integers into strings unless dtype is given; exactly the user_id-must-be-integer dtype-fidelity trap.
Remove dtype from the per-column schema dictionary; maintaining an explicit typed schema over a dataframe, which the merged output needs.
Writer produces an invalid file for a given byte order and string type; correctness of a typed columnar/binary writer, as with the Parquet output.
CSV manager looks up rule keys with the wrong argument; key-based record lookup while consolidating rows from a CSV source.
Invalid characters must be sanitised when exporting to XLSX; output-format constraints in the same multi-format library.
Companion report of the same XLSX sheet-title sanitisation problem; kept for tablib coverage, narrow fix.
Let a data transformer be put into a fitted state from known parameters; column transformation bookkeeping, not merging.
Query over a dataframe fails when grouping by a name column; dataframe field-name handling, only loosely related.

Terminal-Lego-15k.reason: Join three CSVs keyed on a shared person column, each contributing different attribute columns, into one file: the merge core of the TB2.1 task.
Left join silently multiplies rows because the right table has duplicate keys; the classic merge bug that breaks one-row-per-user.
Read several Parquet files in a defined order and write a single combined output; multi-source Parquet ingestion with ordering that matters.
join() fails on overlapping columns and must be replaced by merge() over two real CSVs; choosing the right combine operator for colliding fields.
Convert MM/DD/YYYY strings to datetimes and write them back as ISO YYYY-MM-DD; the exact date normalisation the spec demands.
Read a column holding dates in several different formats and emit one target format; per-source date-format reconciliation.
Convert Parquet to CSV representing NULLs correctly; Parquet null/type semantics, which decide whether optional fields survive the merge.
Read every CSV in a directory and concatenate into one frame; the simplest form of multi-source ingestion, strongly verified.
Drop every row duplicated across a subset of columns, not just the later copies; precise duplicate semantics on a chosen key.
read_csv mislabels columns when usecols, names, index_col and parse_dates are combined; column renaming at parse time going wrong.

Four ingestion sources including a Parquet CRM export and a JSON billing feed, with schema differences causing wrong downstream segmentation.
Three processor exports with different field names and conventions, some transactions present in several files with conflicting values, reconciled into one ledger.

Four regional offices with different tools and conventions consolidated into one clean dataset; the normalise-then-union half of the task.
Reconcile three financial exports with differing conventions and encodings where records appear in all three; cross-source duplicate reconciliation.

CSV, TSV and a fixed-width mainframe export with incompatible schemas mapped onto one unified CRM schema.

notes: CalibForge owns this task: its data-processing category is full of multi-source CRM/ledger consolidation problems with explicit source priority, field-mapping tables, Parquet outputs and JSON reports, and almost all of them are 'strong'-verified with 10-32 pinned assertions. data-processing_20260508_045740_003 is close enough to be nearly the same problem. TMax-15K is a genuine second (three tasks that read CSV+JSON+Parquet and unify schemas), and Terminal-Lego contributes solid, strongly-verified single-step components (three-way CSV join, duplicate-key join blowup, Parquet multi-file read, ISO date conversion) that retrieval had buried behind SQLAlchemy and date-formatting noise. Recursive-Task-Synthesis's best analogue is the base-spec-plus-overrides canonicalisation family, which really does teach priority merging plus a duplicate audit report, but it is all 'absent'-graded so none entered the final ten. TerminalWorld has no true multi-source merge task; its list is format-conversion work and its overall scores reflect that. On the SWE side, the honest transfer is Parquet/date/dtype fidelity (dask parquet round-trip, arrow multi-format parsing, pandas read_json integer coercion) and tablib's ragged-source ingestion, which is the single best SWE-Rebench entry here. Downstream: the packet's verifier field and work/verifier_strength.json disagree on several CalibForge and Terminal-Lego ids (the latter is newer); I used the stricter of the two.
